first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, making simplification the most directly relevant and sustainable intervention. The inherited evidence suggests signup simplification and shorter onboarding improve activation and time-to-value, while avoiding the retention risk associated with promotional pricing. I would verify both records and run a small guarded test, measuring qualified revenue and retention—not just completion or activation—to detect downstream value risk.

final.rationale: Run a segmented simplification experiment for SMB accounts with simple workspaces, focusing on signup friction and nonessential onboarding steps. The verified signup change increased activation 9% and qualified revenue 4%, with only a 1% retention decline. The shortened-flow evidence shows a material 60-day churn increase in complex-workspace accounts, so those accounts must remain on the fuller onboarding path. Monitor completion, activation, qualified revenue, and 30-/60-day retention before expanding.
